attempts.hypothesis: AC-1: a credential-bearing argv[0] still reaches an operator surface (ledger/status and the withheld notice) through displayProgram's own rules.
attempts.method: Executed the committed dist/src/policy.js displayProgram over 59 token templates x 3 credentials, then a targeted battery of exactly the shapes the brief lists (@ before ://, two @, scheme-less userinfo with a port, Windows path, redacts-to-placeholder, empty host part, @ only at the end, whitespace-only), then brute-forced all 32768 tokens of length <=5 over the alphabet {a,@,/,:,.,1,-,space}.
attempts.evidence: Reaches both surfaces (ledger + notice) under the DEFAULT capture mode: displayProgram(["https://alice:hunter2/@db.example.test"]) === "alice:hunter2"; displayProgram(["x@y://alice:hunter2"]) === "alice:hunter2"; displayProgram(["postgres://admin:P/w0rd@db.internal"]) === "admin:P"; displayProgram(["deployer@db.example.test:hunter2"]) === "db.example.test:hunter2". The shapes the brief enumerates are otherwise safe: "alice:hunter2@host:5432" -> "host:5432"; "a@b@c:hunter2@host" -> "host"; "C:\\alice:hunter2@host" -> "host"; "token=abc" -> "token=[REDACTED]"; "alice:hunter2@/x" -> "(no command)"; "alice:hunter2@" -> "(no command)"; whitespace-only / control-only / empty argv -> "(no command)". The 32768-token brute force produced 0 renders containing "@" or "/", so the rendered string is always an @-less, /-less word. NOTE: The renderer's *shape* is what the doc claims; the doc's *scope* statements are what fails (see F1).

attempts.hypothesis: AC-1/AC-5: the withheld path's notice overstates what happened, or fires more than once per session.
attempts.method: Traced noteFirstRun/onWithheldHostAttempt through src/commands.ts:694-698, src/tools.ts:225-228, extensions/index.ts:565-575 and the ledger; compared the notice text with what is actually written, and the slash-command grammar with the tool's schema.
attempts.evidence: The text is accurate (a withheld attempt leaves no host-exec record; the runner path says `audited` only when audit.enabled) and the one-shot flag makes it once per session. But a bare `/devcontainer host-exec` with no argv counts as an attempt and can fire `first host command attempt this session: (no command)`, while the same invocation on an ALLOWED path counts nothing (parseHostExecArgv fails -> usage text, no ledger call, no runner); the tool path cannot produce this because argv has minItems: 1 (src/tools.ts:44) -> finding F4 (nit).

attempts.hypothesis: Brief (d): docs/security.md's residual-scope sentence is exact.
attempts.method: Compared docs/security.md:153-177 against the renderer and against a brute-force search for any render containing "@" or "/".
attempts.evidence: The literal "no @ or /" clause holds (0/32768 renders contained either character), but 'renders the HOST of whatever that token looks like', 'those three gaps matter only under "redacted-text"' and 'which is not a shape a command line produces in practice' do not: a URL-shaped argv[0] whose credential sits before the first `/` puts the user:pass pair on both operator surfaces under the default capture mode (`https://alice:hunter2/@db.example.test` -> `alice:hunter2`) -> finding F1.

findings.message: docs/security.md's 'What the redaction covers, and what it does not' paragraph states that the in-session rendering 'renders the HOST of whatever that token looks like - the authority between `://` and the first `/` (its userinfo dropped)', that the redaction gaps 'matter only under "redacted-text"', and that a credential 'can therefore only reach the operator surfaces by being spelled as a program NAME with no `@` or `/` at all ..., which is not a shape a command line produces in practice'. The renderer emits the pre-slash authority VERBATIM whenever that authority contains no `@`, so a URL-shaped argv[0] with a credential in front of a slash (or with no `@` in the authority at all) puts the credential pair on BOTH operator surfaces under the DEFAULT capture mode (fingerprint-only, no command text recorded): displayProgram(["https://alice:hunter2/@db.example.test"]) === "alice:hunter2", displayProgram(["x@y://alice:hunter2"]) === "alice:hunter2", displayProgram(["postgres://admin:P/w0rd@db.internal"]) === "admin:P" (the slash-in-the-password shape the paragraph itself calls out), displayProgram(["deployer@db.example.test:hunter2"]) === "db.example.test:hunter2"; the leaked value appears in `/devcontainer status` via the ledger and in the one-shot withheld/runner notice. The rendered string is always @-less and /-less (0 of 32768 brute-forced tokens produced a render containing either character), so the code matches AC-1's own definition of the render (the authority between `://` and the first `/`) and this is a documentation-accuracy defect rather than a renderer regression: the paragraph's 'renders the HOST', 'matter only under redacted-text' and 'not a shape a command line produces in practice' clauses need narrowing (or the renderer needs to shave a `user:pass`-shaped authority). The same overstatement appears in CHANGELOG.md ('without creating a place a credential could be rendered'), while src/host-run-ledger.ts itself concedes the truth ('a program name CAN be credential-shaped').

The nit fix in b02dadf ('hostToContainer still hand-rolled the prefix math - the last private segment implementation. It delegates to the shared predicate now') changed behaviour for a mapping whose host side is the filesystem root. hostToContainer('/etc/passwd', {hostPath:'/', containerPath:'/workspaces/proj'}) now returns '/workspaces/projetc/passwd': the root base passes isAtOrUnder, but `${mapping.containerPath}${candidate.slice(host.length)}` (src/path-mapper.ts:103) then slices off the leading separator and the container path has no trailing slash to spare ('/workspaces/proj' + 'etc/passwd'). The pre-revision implementation (git show 8e6b491:src/path-mapper.ts, executed inline) returned undefined for the same call, i.e. 'no mapping' - the safe answer that leaves the host path unchanged. Reachability is narrow but real: buildPathMapping accepts workspaceMount 'source=/,target=/workspace,type=bind' (or a config at /.devcontainer/devcontainer.json), the codebase itself treats {hostPath:'/'} as a legitimate mapping (tests/unit/routing-guards.test.ts:310), and no test covers hostToContainer with a root host side. Impact is presentation-only rather than a routing decision: extensions/index.ts:280 resolveContainerWorkspace feeds ExecOutcome.presentedWorkspace, so a root-mounted workspace at /srv/proj is shown to the agent as '/workspacesrv/proj'. The guard predicate stays shared; only the join needs the root case handled (or path-segment joining instead of a slice).

The only operator-channel surface in this change's blast radius that still interpolates raw input is the unknown-verb diagnostic: extensions/index.ts:715 (dist/extensions/index.js:592) notifies `Unknown /devcontainer verb: ${verb}` with `verb` being the raw first token of the command arguments (lowercased). Every neighbouring surface now routes through the enforced renderer (the withheld notice at extensions/index.ts:571, the free-text refusal at src/commands.ts:836), so a token of exactly the shape this change is about (e.g. `/devcontainer https://alice:hunter2@host`) is echoed verbatim here. It is the operator's own typing and pre-existing (not introduced by this revision), hence a nit - but it is the one remaining raw echo, and `displayProgram([verb])` (or a static message naming the verb picker) would close it.

On the WITHHELD path a bare `/devcontainer host-exec` with no argv is counted as a host-command attempt and can consume the session's one-shot first-attempt notice: src/commands.ts:694-698 calls onWithheldHostAttempt(parseHostExecArgv(args).ok ? argv[0] : args.trim().split(/\s+/)[0] ?? "") before any grammar check, so `args === ""` yields the empty program, the ledger counts 1 and the notice reads 'first host command attempt this session: (no command)'. The same invocation with host execution ALLOWED is not an attempt at all (parseHostExecArgv fails, the usage text is returned, no ledger call, no runner), and the tool surface cannot produce it because argv declares minItems: 1 (src/tools.ts:44) - so the slash-command path over-reports the AC-1 attempt count exactly where a configuration withholds the surface. Cheap fix: treat a failing parse with empty args like the allowed path (usage, no count).
